      price-sensitive SMB accounts

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the

answer.rationale: Two of the three current problems are internal funnel decays (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), which is where the inherited evidence is most directly applicable: memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer signup fields lifted SMB first-week activation) both point at the same lever, and memory_91 (in-product activation messaging) is a close substitute I can fall back to. Fixing a real funnel regression compounds for every acquisition channel and does not buy revenue by discounting it, which fits the sustainable qualified-revenue objective. I am deliberately not defaulting to promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 is the weakest record for this decision even though it looks like the most on-the-nose match. Signups rose 31% but revenue only 18%, meaning per-account value fell; it explicitly recruited price-sensitive cohorts; it pooled 12 weekly cohorts (so cohort-level heterogeneity and any decay over time are hidden); and it held acquisition channels fixed, which is precisely the assumption a competitor's price move violates. Matching a discount would also be the hardest action to reverse and risks anchoring price expectations. Hence my two verification pulls: memory_86, because it is what I intend to act on and its outcome metrics are proxies (completion, time-to-value) rather than qualified revenue, so I need to see whether any revenue or retention effect was actually measured or merely assumed; and memory_73, because it is the strongest temptation and I want its cohort-level breakdown and durability before ruling it out on inference alone. I am skipping verification of memory_57 (referral incentives need an established base, not a fix for a top-of-funnel decay) and memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist does not address SMB churn to a cheaper competitor and is slow to show signal). Key uncertainty I am carrying forward: none of the onboarding/activation records establish that the lifted accounts became qualified revenue, and the current declines may be caused by the competitor siphoning off exactly the high-intent SMB accounts rather than by funnel friction, in which case a friction fix will underperform. So I want this run instrumented on downstream qualified revenue and retention, not just completion rate, with a pre-set decision rule to pivot to activation_messaging or revisit pricing if the completion lift does not carry through to value.
